# QM Intermediate: Course overview {#intermediate-course}

QM Intermediate builds on the probability, inference, and R skills from QM
Basic. The central question changes from "What does this sample show?" to
"How is an outcome related to several variables at the same time?"

::: {.outcomes}
<span class="label">By the end of QM Intermediate, you can</span>

- formulate simple and multiple-regression questions from E&BI problems;
- fit, diagnose, and interpret linear regression models in R;
- distinguish a coefficient, fitted value, residual, and uncertainty
  interval;
- interpret tests against zero, $R^2$, and F-tests for model usefulness;
- use dummy predictors, interactions, and polynomial terms;
- explain how controls change an estimate without automatically making it
  causal;
- read the central regression evidence in a business or management paper.
:::

## How this course connects

Expectation and variance become the foundations for regression coefficients
and residual variation. Covariance and correlation motivate linear
relationships, while the inference tools from Basic return when we quantify
uncertainty around model estimates.

The Shark Tank data continue as the main shared example, with money amounts
measured in thousands of dollars throughout so that axes and coefficients
stay readable. Additional datasets are not required for the core sequence.

## Course sequence

| Chapter | Central question |
|---|---|
| Lecture 1 | What line best summarises the relationship between two variables? |
| Lecture 2 | What does the model assume, and what do its residuals confess? |
| Lecture 3 | How precise are the coefficients, and is the model useful at all? |
| Tutorial 1 | Can you fit, diagnose, and communicate a simple regression? |
| Lecture 4 | How do we interpret one predictor while holding others fixed? |
| Lecture 5 | How do categories enter a model, and are terms jointly useful? |
| Lecture 6 | When does a slope depend on another variable or change across $x$? |
| Tutorial 2 | Can you build and defend a multiple-regression specification? |
| Code sheet | Which R commands and formulas are required for the assessment? |
| Mock exam | Can you integrate the complete course in a 100-point assessment? |

External video explanations come from Stanford's
[Statistical Learning series](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoROMvodv4rOzrYsAxzQyHb8n_RWNuS1e).
The supporting print text is James, Witten, Hastie, and Tibshirani,
*An Introduction to Statistical Learning*, 2nd edition, especially Chapter 3.
For a more formal treatment, consult
[Nieuwenhuis, *Statistical Methods for Business and Economics*](https://tilburguniversity.on.worldcat.org/oclc/317545871),
especially Chapters 19--22. Each lecture chapter contains the definitions,
notation, examples, and practice required for this course.

## The weekly rhythm

One lecture per week, with tutorials the day after the lecture in weeks 45
and 48. The [How to succeed in this course](../resources/how-to-succeed.qmd)
page lays out the cycle with printable checklists, including the deliberate
ordering of tutorial preparation.

## Tutorials and assessment

Two tutorials---one after Lecture 3 and one after Lecture 6---combine
interpretation with hands-on R work. They prepare you to work with data in R
during the TestVision assessment. If an R workflow has become rusty, return
to the [R Refresher](../resources/r-refresher.qmd) or the earlier
[Programming for E&BI](https://walshc.github.io/ebi-prog/) textbook.

Use the cumulative [QM Intermediate Code Sheet](code-sheet.qmd) throughout
the tutorials and when preparing for the final exam. After completing
Tutorial 2, attempt the [QM Intermediate Mock Exam](mock-exam.qmd) in R under
timed conditions.
